audit_scope.description: This batch covers CL P2P gossip/request-response protocols (Phase0), CL fork upgrades (EIP-7441 Whisk), CL inclusion lists (EIP-7805), CL serialization (SSZ), EL difficulty calculation (Muir Glacier), EL hard fork activation (EIP-609 Byzantium), EL empty account prohibition (EIP-7523), EL LOG opcodes (Cancun), EL wallet RPC (EIP-747), and EIP governance process (EIP-1).

out_of_scope: EIP Governance Process (EIP-1, meta-process not runtime protocol)

execution_layer.threat: Submit malformed transactions, request wallet track phishing tokens via wallet_watchAsset, SSRF via image URLs
Send blocks with invalid difficulty, trigger undefined behavior with empty accounts, eclipse attacks

consensus_layer.threat: Submit conflicting inclusion lists (equivocation), send invalid attestations/blocks, Sybil attack on gossip mesh
Send malformed SSZ payloads, oversized messages, eclipse attacks, decompression bombs
Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal node component responsible for block processing, not an external entity. Resides within the EL client.
EIP governance process participant, not a runtime protocol entity. EIP-1 describes a meta-process, not protocol-level data flow.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via CL Gossip (GossipSub)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P gossip network. Any peer can send messages on subscribed topics. Messages may be malformed, oversized, or maliciously crafted. Peer identity provides no trust guarantee.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Beacon Node via Req/Resp Protocol
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P connection. Peers are discovered via discv5 and connected via libp2p. Fork digest check provides compatibility verification but not trust. Peer may send invalid responses, incorrect status, or attempt resource exhaustion.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via EL P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer sending block headers and bodies. Blocks may have invalid difficulty, incorrect fork rules, or malformed transactions. No authentication mechanism.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners produce blocks with difficulty calculations. A malicious miner could attempt to submit blocks with incorrect difficulty values. Block difficulty must be fully validated against the expected computation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via P2P (Inclusion List Submission)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators submit inclusion lists via P2P. A validator may equivocate by sending conflicting inclusion lists for the same slot. Equivocation detection is required. Lists must arrive before view freeze deadline.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Builder (EIP-7805 context)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block building interface consuming inclusion list transactions
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block builders consume inclusion list transactions but may attempt to censor or reorder them. Enforcement mechanism for inclusion is separate from the list submission protocol.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web Application (dApp) via wallet_watchAsset RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any website can invoke wallet_watchAsset. dApps may attempt phishing by requesting tracking of tokens that impersonate legitimate assets. Image URLs may target internal services (SSRF). Response timing must not leak wallet state (fingerprinting).

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted SSZ Data Source via P2P/RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: SSZ deserialization pipeline (P2P messages, RPC responses, stored snapshots)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Raw SSZ bytes from any external source are untrusted. Malformed payloads may exploit deserialization: invalid offsets, excess trailing bytes, list capacity violations, invalid union selectors, missing bitlist sentinels, or decompression bombs.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All gossip messages must be decompressed (snappy), size-validated (<= 10 MiB), message-ID computed, and content-validated per topic-specific rules (signature, slot, committee). REJECT messages penalize peer score.
Oversized messages must be dropped and sender penalized via peer scoring. Snappy decompression must enforce size limit before full decompression to prevent memory exhaustion.
Message timestamps must be within 500ms tolerance. Messages from the future beyond this window must be IGNORED (not REJECTED) to avoid penalizing peers with slight clock drift.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: libp2p connection handler with mandatory Status exchange
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork digest must be compared on connection. Mismatched fork digests require immediate disconnect. Status fields (finalized checkpoint, head) must not be blindly trusted for chain state decisions.

Block difficulty must be independently computed from parent header and compared against claimed difficulty. Difficulty bomb delay offset (9,000,000 for Muir Glacier) must be correctly applied. Invalid difficulty must cause block rejection.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block validation with fork-specific rules (EIP-609 Byzantium activation)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block number must be checked against fork activation threshold to select correct validation ruleset. All 9 Byzantium EIPs must activate atomically at the fork block. Blocks from non-upgraded peers on different rules must be rejected.

Block number used for difficulty calculation must be the canonical chain height. The bomb delay offset must be applied correctly (max(0, block_number - 9,000,000)). Integer underflow must be prevented via clamping to zero.

Inclusion lists must be received before view freeze deadline. Equivocation (conflicting lists from same validator for same slot/root) must be detected and the validator's lists excluded from aggregation. Transactions must be deduplicated.
Block builders must be constrained by separate enforcement mechanisms to actually include required transactions. The inclusion list store must correctly exclude equivocators from the transaction set.

Request must be validated: asset type recognized, address checksum verified, chain ID validated. Image URLs must be checked for dangerous schemes (file://, http://) and SSRF (localhost/internal targets). Token similarity must be checked against known token lists for phishing. Response must be returned before user interaction to prevent fingerprinting.

All SSZ deserialization must validate: offset ordering and range, no excess trailing bytes, list capacity limits, union selector bounds (0-127), bitlist sentinel presence. Malformed data must be rejected. Implementations should enforce maximum nesting depth to prevent stack overflow.

Raw SSZ bytes must be deserialized with full validation before use in consensus logic. Deserialization failures must not cause crashes or undefined behavior. Memory allocation during deserialization must be bounded by declared type limits.

coverage_analysis.notes: 4 entities from subgraph files were reclassified as misclassified (EXT-BLOCK-PROCESSOR is internal; EXT-AUTHOR, EXT-EIP-EDITOR, EXT-CORE-DEVS are governance-process entities outside protocol runtime). 3 files (EIP-7441, EIP-7523, Cancun LOG) had no external entities, consistent with their internal-only state transition nature.
